messages:
Alex Turner: Quick sync: onboarding new private/VPC customer this week. Need a short, copy-pasteable list of endpoints + example configs for OTLP (traces/metrics), Prom remote_write, and log forwarding. Also which read-only Grafana dashboards do we share? @Maria Chen, can you confirm?

Maria Chen: Yep. Short list I hand out:
1) OTLP ingestion endpoint + short-lived token via onboarding flow. Example we give customers:
```
OTLP endpoint: https://otlp.prod-redwood.net/vpc/<vpc-id>/ingest
Header: Authorization: Bearer <short-lived-token>
```
2) Prometheus remote_write to our metrics gateway (TLS, bearer token). Example snippet:
```yaml
remote_write:
  - url: "https://metrics-gateway.prod-redwood.net/v1/write/<customer-id>"
    bearer_token: "<token-from-onboard>"
    tls_config:
      insecure_skip_verify: false
```
3) Logs: prefer structured JSON via OTLP using promtail/loki-compatible forwarder or our TCP log-forwarder. If they must use syslog, we accept it but advise mapping to our resource attributes (tenant_id, service.name).

Kevin Park: Add a note on telemetry sampling and resource attributes. If resource.service.name is missing dashboards get messy. Also for prom_remote_write_errors include this config in their prometheus to reduce cardinality: relabel_configs to drop debug labels.

Priya Singh: For dashboards I maintain three tenant-level read-only panels we typically share (read-only links):
- https://grafana.redwood.net/d/alpha123/customer-latency?orgId=1&var-tenant=cust-XXX
- https://grafana.redwood.net/d/beta456/customer-throughput?orgId=1&var-tenant=cust-XXX
- https://grafana.redwood.net/d/gamma789/ingest-pipeline-health?orgId=1&var-tenant=cust-XXX
Put a note that these are read-only and behind tenant scoping.

Alex Turner: Good. Alerting: customer reports spikes in token errors. Who do I ping to review thresholds and possible false positives?

Maria Chen: Ping @Kevin Park and @observability-bot with tenant id + a sample trace id. We have an automation that snapshots current alerts for the tenant. If it's noisy we can relax threshold or add aggregation/grouping.

observability-bot: Automation: snapshot for tenant cust-412 returned 2 firing alerts: high_token_errors, p99_latency_spike. Dashboard links: https://alerts.redwood.net/tenant/cust-412. Include recent trace IDs for context.

Kevin Park: I'll triage. Quick checklist for you to ask the customer before adjusting alerts:
- Are token errors tied to a specific model or route?
- Is there traffic burst pattern (cron/batch)?
- Are there corresponding prom_remote_write_errors?
If it's operational noise from retries we prefer to increase the alert window or require sustained firing for 5m -> 15m.

Priya Singh: Also recommend enabling span sampling at onboarding to get traces quickly (first 48h at 100% then drop to default). Otherwise they may send spans and think nothing ingested.

Alex Turner: One more: IAM/permissions. What role allows customers to only see their tenant dashboards? Read-only only.

Maria Chen: Use the tenant_readonly role. It scopes Grafana API keys to tenant id and denies data outside that tenant. I can paste the snippet for creating an API key in the console. Also note that keys are short-lived by default for private VPCs.

Kevin Park: If they want programmatic key rotation point them to /v1/tenant/keys in the private control plane API. We support key rotation via the console or API.

Alex Turner: Perfect. I'll update the onboarding doc with these snippets and include the checklist: test span, push sample metric, ship a log line, confirm grafana link, confirm alerts snapshot. Will ping for review when done. :thumbsup:

Maria Chen: Thanks! Please add the resource.service.name reminder and the sample relabel_config for Prom.

Priya Singh: And add a note to enable structured fields (tenant_id, model_name, route) in logs so the dashboards can filter reliably.

Kevin Park: lgtm, ping me when you want the alert thresholds set.

Alex Turner: Will do. Thanks everyone.
